title: Authorized connections between tenants
description:
Departments inside one deployment need to work together, so tenants need a way to reach each other. This is the feature that punches a hole in the only hard boundary the design has, so it is specified now and built after the authority epic.

`{tenant_id}#channel#{id}` is a physical partition. A connection is a deliberate, narrow exception built from the clip primitive that already exists.

**Four rules, from docs/ORGANIZATIONS.md:**

- Grants name a resource, never a tenant. Support may read this channel is a connection; support may reach Legal is a merge.
- A connection is clipped twice: by the granting member's ceiling, and by what the tenant's owner permits to leave the tenant at all.
- Received authority is borrowed, not owned, which is what makes connections non-transitive. B cannot re-share A's grant with C because B never held it. Without that distinction the boundary leaks one hop at a time.
- Never at the workplace level. A connection reaches a channel or a named resource, never the computer. A shared workplace across tenants collapses the boundary rather than opening a door in it.

**Blocked by the authority epic ba3ea4.** A connection is a clip, and the clip has to exist first.
